transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because things at work have been feeling off ever since I got that county safety award. I’m a transportation inspector, and since then, certain people have been twisting what I put in my inspection reports. They’ll ask these pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look like I’m doing something crooked.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but… I don’t buy that. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Are you certain these people are deliberately trying to discredit you?

Yes. I mean, I can’t prove every single thing, but it’s too consistent to be normal. Ever since I got that safety award, my reports get questioned in a way they didn’t before, and the budget questions feel like they’re trying to make me look dishonest. My supervisor says it’s routine review, but I can tell there’s something coordinated going on to discredit me.
Have you noticed anything that you see as clear evidence that people at work are conspiring against you?

The clearest thing is how my inspection reports started getting picked apart after the safety award. Not just normal corrections—people twisting what I wrote, then coming back with these budget questions that make it sound like I’m hiding something or doing something crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just routine review, but the timing and the way they’re doing it feels coordinated to me.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?
No, I haven’t heard voices when nobody was there. It’s not like that.
If your supervisor showed you clear proof that the reviews were routine, would you believe it?

I’d look at it, but honestly, I don’t know if I’d just accept it. Ever since that safety award, my reports have been twisted and the budget questions feel pointed, like they’re trying to make me look crooked. So even if my supervisor showed me paperwork saying it’s routine, I’d still wonder if that’s just how they’re covering it.
Do you feel that people outside of your workplace are also trying to harm, watch, or discredit you?

No, not really outside work. It’s mainly certain people at work. Since that county safety award, my inspection reports keep getting twisted and these budget questions come up like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s normal review, but it feels coordinated to me.
Has anything happened that would be impossible or extremely unlikely in ordinary life, like people controlling your thoughts or sending you special messages?

No, nothing like people controlling my thoughts or sending me messages. It’s more… at work, after that county safety award, certain people started twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions. It feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked, like there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me, even though my supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review.
Aside from this issue at work, have you had trouble functioning in the rest of your life?

Not really, no. I mean, I still get to work on time, I do my inspections, I take care of myself. I still go to church and keep up with things. The trouble mostly starts when those reports come up, or when people start questioning my spending like there’s something wrong. That’s when it gets hard.
How long have you been convinced that these people at work are trying to discredit you?
About a year now, I’d say. It started after I got recognized for that county safety initiative, and since then I’ve been pretty convinced they’ve been trying to discredit me.
Before this started at work, have you generally tended to distrust other people and suspect they had harmful motives?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with people, but I wouldn’t say I went around assuming everybody was out to hurt me. This work situation is what really changed things for me.
During this past year, have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energetic, or elated for days at a time?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve had times I was stressed or worked up about things, but not like unusually high or elated for days.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?
No, not really. I mean, I haven’t seen things that other people couldn’t see.
Do you feel that ordinary things, like conversations, TV, or events around you, are meant to refer specifically to you?

Not TV or random things like that, no. It’s more at work. Since I got that county safety award, certain people started twisting my inspection reports, and then they ask these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal to me. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are deliberately trying to discredit you?

Yes. I mean, I can’t prove every single piece of it, but I’m certain there’s something coordinated going on. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel that way to me. I can tell they’re trying to discredit me.
Over the past year, have you noticed yourself becoming emotionally flat or losing motivation in general?

I don’t think so. I mean, I still get up and go to work, take care of what I need to. I wouldn’t say I’ve felt emotionally flat. Maybe stressed sometimes, but not like I’ve lost motivation in general.
Just before this started, did something particularly stressful happen in your life?
Not that I can think of. I mean, work is always a little stressful, but I don’t remember some big event right before it started. It just kind of developed.
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about your coworkers trying to discredit you?

I guess anything is possible in theory, but no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my reports and asking those pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell it’s coordinated.
Has anyone you trust told you that your belief about your coworkers might not be true?

Yes. My supervisor has said it’s just normal review and that I’m reading too much into it. But I don’t buy that. Since I got that county safety award, certain coworkers have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. It feels coordinated.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts are hard to follow or seem jumbled?
No, not really. I mean, nobody’s told me I’m hard to follow or that I’m not making sense. I think I explain things pretty clearly.
During this past year, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t think so. I’ve had stressful days and times I was upset, but I can’t say there was a stretch of two weeks where I felt depressed most of the day every day.
